rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited covenant warning says those who abandon God’s covenant incur anger, curse, destruction, and exile; later generations identify the broken covenant as the cause.
rows.anchor: تركوا عهد الله إله آبائهم , فاشتد غضب الرب عن بلادهم بغضب وزجحر شديد ويبعدهم إلى أرض غريبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The captivity that followed their punishment caused God to disperse them extensively across the earth into many separate groups.
rows.anchor: بسبب ما حصل لهم من السبي المترتب على العذاب بما لنا من العظمة تقطيعا كثيرا بأن أكثرنا تفريقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few lived in each town, leaving them without collective strength or the ability to defend themselves against oppression.
rows.anchor: فصار في كل بلدة قليل منهم ليست لهم شوكة ولا يدفعون عن أنفسهم ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous remained on their religion until its abrogating dispensation came, then followed it in obedience to the call of their own scripture.
rows.anchor: الذين ثبتوا على دينهم إلى أن جاء الناسخ له فتبعوه امتثالا لدعوة كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others fell below that standing, sometimes through wickedness and sometimes through disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي بالفسق تارة وبالكفر أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested them with blessings and calamities in hope that desire for good or fear of harm would bring them back.
rows.anchor: { بالحسنات } اي النعم { والسئات } اي النقم { لعلهم يرجعون } أي ليكون حالهم حال من يرجى رجوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowly, near display is worldly life; they persist without repentance and confidently assume they will be forgiven.
rows.anchor: أي دائما من غير توبة . ولما كان النافع الغفران من غير نظر إلى معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If another equally base and illicit gain, such as a bribe, comes to them, they take it again.
rows.anchor: في الدناءة ولخسة - والحرمة كالرشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They use the passive form because they seek assurance of forgiveness without naming or considering a particular forgiver.
rows.anchor: من غير نظر إلى معين , بنوا للمفعول قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The binding covenant in the Torah requires them to speak only truth about God; asserting certain forgiveness without repentance is not established truth and violates it.
rows.anchor: { ميثاق الكتاب } اي الميثاق المؤكد في التوارة { أن لا يقولوا } أي قولا من الأقوال وإن قل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeatedly read and memorized the covenant, so they could not excuse their conduct by claiming ignorance of what their forebears received.
rows.anchor: أي ما في ذلك الميثاق بتكرير القراءة للحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their scripture teaches that the afterlife is better than the worldly gains they take; they choose what harms and vanishes over lasting good.
rows.anchor: أي فعلوا ما تقدم من مجانبة التقوى والحال أن الآخرة { خير } أي مما يأخذون { للذين يتقون } أي هم يعملون ذلك بإخبار كتابهم

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحفص
rows.claim: On the address-form reading, the question directly addresses them and signals the extremity of divine anger.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة نافع وابن عامر وحفص بالخطاب يكون المارد الإعلام بتناهي الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocation is bound to worship: the polytheists invoke their idols as objects of worship, and calling is inseparable from the one worshipped.
rows.anchor: أي أيها المشركون كون دعاء عبادة ملازمين لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, invocation is used for worship to show that one incapable of being invoked cannot rightly be worshipped.
rows.anchor: أو أنه أطلق الدعاء على العبادة إشارة إلى أنه لا تصح عبادة من ليس فيه قابيلة أن يدعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are powerless servants like their worshippers, especially unable to meet the Qur’an’s challenge; humans surpass them in life and reason, while a true deity cannot be like a worshipper.
rows.anchor: أي في العجز عن كل شيء لا سيما عما وقع بع التحدي من معارضة القرآن وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is to call them to anything and see if they answer clearly, produce a comparable surah, or provide any benefit; a true god would answer a devotee.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإله الحق يجيب وليه عند التحدي من غير تخلف

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads إن lightly and عبادا أمثالكم with the accusative, treating إن as a negative particle that raises its noun and sets its predicate in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير { إن } خفيفة و { عبادا أمثالكم بنصب الدال واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians dispute whether إن may work like الحجازية ما: al-Kisāʾī, most Kufans, Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Fārisī, and Ibn Jinnī allow it; al-Farrāʾ and most Basrans reject it, with reports differing on Sibawayh and al-Mubarrad.
rows.anchor: وإعمالها هذا العمل فيه خلاف , أجازه الكسائي وأكثر الكوفيين , ومن البصريين ابن السراج والفارسي وابن جني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī holds that this grammatical use of إن is a documented language found in both verse and prose.
rows.anchor: والصيحح أن إعمالها لغة ثبت ذلك في النظم والنثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative reading need not conflict with the familiar affirmative: affirmation concerns shared incapacity, while denial concerns equality, since people exceed idols in other capacities.
rows.anchor: وليس الأمر هنا كذلك , فالاثبات لمماثلتها لهم في مطلق العجز

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī resolves the readings by taking the affirmative as concessive and the negation as the literal truth.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري - أن الإثبات على سبيل التنزل والنفي على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunting questions proceed through movement, striking, sight, and hearing: movement is the first feared action, then assault, then seeing danger, then hearing a threat from afar or out of sight.
rows.anchor: مقدما الأجل لأن أول ما يخشى من الشيء انتقاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to possess these capacities makes the idols inferior to humans and effectively nonexistent in themselves; any capacity they have is granted by their maker.
rows.anchor: لزم نقصانها عنهم وأنه في الحقيقة مسلوب عنهم لأنهم ليس لهم من ذواتهم إلا العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet challenges them and their partners together to plot against him, despite their multitude and his solitude, and not to delay even a moment.
rows.anchor: أي جميعا أنتم وهم وأنتم أكثر من حصى البطحاء ورمل الفضاء وأنا وحدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Prophet’s supporter and governor, the one who progressively sent the comprehensive Book, whose contents the idolaters and their partners cannot rival.
rows.anchor: أي بحسب التديج متكفلا بفصل الوقائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book’s unmatched revelation is verbal evidence of God’s life, will, power, knowledge, hearing, sight, and speech; the idolaters’ inability to rival it is evidence against their claims.
rows.anchor: وهي الحياة التامه المستلزمه للإدراة والقدرة والعلم والسمع والبصر والكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continuously protects every righteous person; the surah’s earlier accounts show Him saving allies and destroying enemies, returning this argument to the command to follow revelation rather than other patrons.
rows.anchor: وهو دال على أنه الذي فعل ما تقدم لأجل أوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember the Lord inwardly with understanding and practice; concealed remembrance better supports sincerity, reflection, and vigilant awareness of divine nearness.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرا يكون راسخا فيك مظروفا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance should express humility without loud clamoring, like discreet speech to a ruler; a voice below public loudness better serves sincerity.
rows.anchor: أي لأنه أدخل في الإخلاص

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told companions who had raised their voices excessively that they were not calling someone deaf or absent.
rows.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للصحابة وقد جهروا بالدعاء فوق المقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal remembrance helps the heart remember; hearing oneself is enough to affect imagination and strengthen inward remembrance.
rows.anchor: فإن المقصود حصول الذكر اللساني ليعين الذكر القلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As remembrance deepens, its lights reflect and increase, carrying the seeker from bodily darkness toward the light of the Lord of light and darkness.
rows.anchor: ولا تزال الأنوار تتزايد فينعكس تراجع بعضها إلى بعض حتى يزداد الترقي من ظلمات عالم الأجسام إلى أنوار مدبر النور والظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī suggests الغدو is singular as a verbal noun of غدا; another view treats it as the plural of غدوة, including morning and forenoon.
rows.anchor: أي أوقات البكر , ولعله أفرده علىجعله مصدر غدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second grammatical account takes الغدو as plural of غدوة, so it can include the morning and forenoon.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الغدو وجمع غدوة , فيراد حينئذ مع الصبح الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣīl names the end of each day because it joins the beginning of the following night and day.
rows.anchor: وآخر كل نهار متصل بأول ليلة اليوم الثاني فسمي آخر اليوم أصيلا لأنه يتصل بما هو أصل اليوم الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the command means constant remembrance, it names dawn and evening as parts representing the whole day and night: dawn recalls emergence from death, evening stillness and return to nonexistence.
rows.anchor: وخص هذين الوقتين وإن كان المراد الدوام بتسمية كل من اليوم والليل باسم جزئه , ليذكر بالغدو الانتشار من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two named times do not restrict the command: remember God at every time and in every state.
rows.anchor: أي في غيرهما , بل كن ذاكره في كل وقت على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord are the pure, protected angels; their nearness is rank and station, not physical location.
rows.anchor: وهم الملائكة الكرام أولو العصمة , والقرب دنو مكانة لا مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neither display nor seek pride in worship, despite their closeness, purity, and love.
rows.anchor: أي لا يوجدون ولا يطلبون الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their tasbīḥ declares God free of everything unfitting, and their purity removes the pull of desire and self-interest.
rows.anchor: أي ينزهونه عن كل مالا يليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels reserve prostration for God, combining affirmation of His perfection with direct bodily worship.
rows.anchor: أي يخضعون بإثباتهم له كل كمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gives three angelic traits: freedom from pride, glorification, and exclusive prostration; inward glorification and bodily prostration represent heart and physical worship.
rows.anchor: وقد تضمنت الآية الإخبار عن الملائكة الأبرار بثلاثة أخبار : عدم الاستكبار الذي هو أجل أنواع العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the saying that a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating; Abū Ḥayyān notes that both forms of worship ultimately return to the heart, one signaled by speech and the other by action.
rows.anchor: ( أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد ) نبه عليه أبو حيان على أن العبادتين مرجعهما القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ humility and regular submission contrast with Iblīs’s arrogant refusal to prostrate to Adam; the surah’s conclusion also returns to its opening command to follow the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: إلى وصف إبليس بعصيان أمر الله في السجود لآدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verse about those created for Hell returns to the opening description that the bad land yields only poor growth.
rows.anchor: هو قوله 77 ( { والذي خبث لا يخرج إلا نكدا } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 58 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call upon God by His beautiful names echoes the earlier command to call upon Him humbly and privately.
rows.anchor: ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 180 ] هو - { ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community that guides by truth is associated with the earlier description of believers who do good and inherit Paradise.
rows.anchor: ممن خلقنا أمة يهدون بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing account also recalls the earlier description of those who deny God’s signs and act arrogantly.
rows.anchor: والذين كذبوا بآيتنا واستكبروا عنها } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 36 ]

words: وَإِنْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَدِ ٱقْتَرَبَ أَجَلُهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that their term may be near echoes the rule that a people’s appointed term cannot be delayed.
rows.anchor: وإن عسى أن يكون قد اقترب أجلهم } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 185 ] هو 77 ( { إذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 34 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the Hour is connected to resurrection as at creation, humanity’s earthly dwelling until its term, creation from one soul, and the initial creation and formation.
rows.anchor: يسئلونك عن الساعة } ) 77 [ النازعات : 42 ] هو 77 ( { كما بدأكم تعودون } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 29 ]

words: إِنَّمَآ أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ مِن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rejecting rival gods, the closing declaration of following revelation returns to the opening command to follow the Book and not other patrons.
rows.anchor: إنما أتبع ما يوحى إلي من ربي } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 203 ] - إلى آخرها بعد التنفير من الأنداد - هو كتاب أنزل إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group may be pardoned because it is suited to repentance, while a sizeable group is punished for persistent criminality.
rows.anchor: أي لصلاحيتها للتوبة { تعذب طائفة } أي قوم ذوو عدد

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads both verbs in the active voice, using the majestic plural for their subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ببناء الفعلين للفاعل على العظمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the mockers ridiculed Muhammad’s claim that he would defeat the Romans and conquer their cities.
rows.anchor: قيل : كانوا يقولون : إن محمدا يزعم أنه يغلب الروم ويفتح مدائنهم , ما أبعده من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says they claimed that the Qur’an about their companions in Medina was merely Muhammad’s own speech.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يقولون : إن محمدا يزعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God informed the Prophet; he summoned the men, confronted them with what they had said, and they answered that they had only been talking and joking as travelers do to pass the road.
rows.anchor: احسبوا الركب علي , فدعاهم وقال لهم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq identifies the sole man pardoned as Makhshī ibn Ḥumayr al-Ashjaʿī: he laughed but did not join the mockery, disapproved as he walked beside them, repented, and later died at Yamāma after praying for martyrdom.
rows.anchor: قال ابن اسحاق : والذي عفى عنه رجل واحد وهو مخشي بن حمير الأسجعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī suggests calling the pardoned man a faction honors and protects him while signaling that others repented too.
rows.anchor: ولعل إطلاقا الطائفة عليه تعظيما له وسترا عليه وتبشيرا بتوبة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He conjectures that Makhshī had wavering faith, making “after your faith” especially shaming among Arabs who praise steadfastness; al-Jullās and others in the later account may not have believed until repentance, hence “after their Islam.”
rows.anchor: ولعل مخشيا كان مؤمنا ولكن كان إيمانه مزلزلا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān quotes Ibn ʿUmar seeing Wadīʿa ibn Thābit clinging to the Prophet’s camel strap and repeating the excuse while stones struck him; the Prophet answered with the verse’s rebuke.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قال ابن عمر : رأيت وديعة بن ثابت متعلقا بحقب ناقة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female hypocrites share one nature, like a single body, resembling each other in every act and condition through shared desire, habit, custom, and imitation.
rows.anchor: أي في صفة النفاق هم فيها كالجسد الواحد , أمورهم متشابهة في أقوالهم وأفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promote mischief and other vile conduct, oppose what honors Islam and its people, and do so to stir up discord.
rows.anchor: أي مما تقدم من الخبال والإيضاع في الخلال وغير ذلك من سيء الخصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They clutch back their wealth and spend only reluctantly.
rows.anchor: أي يحشون فلا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forgetting God means treating the supreme sovereign as irrelevant; His “forgetting” them is leaving them outside mercy, bringing punishment.
rows.anchor: فعل بهم فعل الناسي لما استهان به بأن تركهم من رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They alone are fully characterized as fāsiqūn: firmly outside the sphere of obedience that benefits them.
rows.anchor: أي الخارجون عن دائرة ما ينفعهم من الطاعة الراسخون في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all hypocrites share one character, the unpardoned men would have behaved the same way if they had gone on campaign.
rows.anchor: فقد علم أنهم لو غزوا فعلوا هؤلاء سواء لأن الكل من طينة واحدة

words: أَلَمْ يَأْتِهِمْ نَبَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing hypocrites’ pursuit of immediate enjoyment and warning of punishment, the passage cites earlier peoples as a warning about what befell their counterparts.
rows.anchor: ولما قرر سبحانه بهذه الآية تشابههم في التمتع بالعاجل , وختمها بهذا الختام المؤذن بالانتقام , اتبع ذلك بتخويفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people enjoyed long lives, lasting traces, and pleasant lands, but the flood destroyed them, leaving no disbeliever alive.
rows.anchor: { قوم نوح } أي في طول اعمارهم وامتداد آثارهم وطيب قرارهم بحسن التمتع في أرضهم وديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd were physically powerful, prestigious, builders, and tyrannical; the furious wind destroyed their unbelievers.
rows.anchor: { وعاد } أي في قوة أبدانهم وعظيم شأنهم ومصانعهم وبنيانهم وتجبرهم في عظيم سلطانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd occupied the extensive region of al-Ḥijr, mountains and plains, but an earthquake destroyed their unbelievers.
rows.anchor: { ثمود * } أي في تمكنهم من بلاد الحجر عرضها وطولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people had dominion across the earth, yet God stripped them of it after severe destruction.
rows.anchor: { قوم إبراهيم } أي في ملك جميع الأرض بطولها والعرض , سلب الله منهم الملك بعد شديد الهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midianites amassed wealth and pursued unlawful as well as lawful gain, cheating in weights and measures, so God punished them collectively.
rows.anchor: { وأصحاب مدين } أي في جمع الأموال ومد الآمال إلى أخذها من حرام وحلال ونقص الميزان والمكيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overturned cities’ people neglected chastity for their desires and were wholly destroyed after the land was overturned beneath them.
rows.anchor: { والمؤتفكات } اي في إعراضهم عن صيانة أعراضهم في اتباع لذائذ أغراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each people received its messenger and clear miracles; God did not destroy them unjustly or without warning, but they rejected the signs and brought ruin on themselves, so the audience is warned to repent.
rows.anchor: أي أتى كل أمة منهم رسولها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that these peoples are singled out because Arabs knew their histories, their lands were nearby, their numbers were great, and their prophets were among the greatest.
rows.anchor: مع أنهم كانوا أكثر الأمم عددا , وأنبياؤهم أعظم الأنبياء - نبه على ذلك أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests Midian precedes Lot’s people despite chronology because the sequence highlights the failure of refuges: Noah’s pyramids, ʿĀd’s houses and fortresses, and Thamūd’s mountain dwellings could not shield them from their punishments.
rows.anchor: لعله قدم أصحاب مدين على قوم لوط وهم فيه بعدهم في الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ mutual alliance and their commands to good, rejection of wrong, prayer, almsgiving, and obedience stand as the faithful pattern beside the warning about earlier disbelieving peoples.
rows.anchor: والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أوليآء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ سَيَرْحَمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful are promised God’s mercy, while His might and wisdom ground the promise.
rows.anchor: أولئك سيرحمهم الله إن الله عزيز حكيم
